tasks.title: [Research] Propose a pain-point taxonomy for the synthetic scenarios
tasks.outcome: A documented v1 taxonomy and labels for 12 synthetic questions
tasks.body:
## Why this matters
The workflow needs a small, explainable taxonomy before model classification can be evaluated.

## Allowed inputs
Use only `examples/ownership-code/synthetic-scenarios.json`, `docs/CHALLENGE.md`, and public sources you cite. Do not add real people, private groups, or prospect data.

## Deliverable
Create `research/pain-point-taxonomy-v1.md` with: category names and definitions; inclusion/exclusion rules; one label for each scenario; ambiguous cases; and limitations.

## Completion criteria
- [ ] Every scenario has a proposed label and short rationale
- [ ] Categories are distinguishable and do not claim sensitive traits
- [ ] Ambiguity and reviewer disagreement are documented
- [ ] PR links this Issue and passes the data/safety checklist

## Claim this task
Comment with your proposed categories or method, expected date/time zone, and help needed.

tasks.title: [Design] Sketch the human-review and handoff states
tasks.outcome: An accessible wireframe for approve, revise, reject, and human takeover
tasks.body:
## Why this matters
Human judgment is a required system boundary, not a decorative approval button.

## Deliverable
Add `docs/design/review-states.md` with a low-fidelity diagram or HTML mockup showing draft, evidence, uncertainty, approve, revise, reject, ask-for-context, and human-takeover states. Include keyboard and small-screen considerations.

## Constraints
Use synthetic text only. Do not design automatic sending or make AI look like a specific person.

## Completion criteria
- [ ] All required states and the next action are visible
- [ ] Evidence and uncertainty are reviewable before approval
- [ ] No action sends externally
- [ ] At least one newcomer can follow the flow from the document

## Claim this task
Comment with your format, expected date/time zone, and help needed.

tasks.title: [Evaluation] Define the first fixture and result schema
tasks.outcome: JSON Schema or documented schema for safe, reproducible fixtures and results
tasks.body:
## Why this matters
Comparable experiments require versioned inputs, provenance, expected safety flags, model metadata, and reviewer outcomes.

## Deliverable
Propose schemas under `evaluation/schema/` for an input fixture and evaluation result. Add two valid synthetic examples and document validation.

## Required fields
Opaque ID, provenance, allowed use, question, source-card IDs, expected risk flags, workflow/model version, reviewer action, rubric scores, Token/cost estimate, and limitations. No personal data.

## Completion criteria
- [ ] Examples validate using a documented command or manual procedure
- [ ] Schema supports the rubric in `docs/EVALUATION.md`
- [ ] Personal contact fields are intentionally absent
- [ ] Provider-specific metadata is optional and portable

## Claim this task
Comment with JSON Schema or alternative approach, expected date/time zone, and help needed.

tasks.title: [Engineering] Implement a provider-neutral mock workflow contract
tasks.outcome: A no-network mock flow from synthetic input to reviewable draft
tasks.body:
## Goal
Implement the smallest no-network path described in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: validate input, assign a placeholder pain-point label, select fixture sources, produce a draft with uncertainty, and return a human-review action.

## Constraints
No paid API, browser automation, external outreach, private data, or production connector. Agree on language/runtime in this Issue before implementation.

## Completion criteria
- [ ] A documented command runs on at least two synthetic fixtures
- [ ] Output includes evidence IDs, uncertainty, and review status
- [ ] Tests cover invalid provenance and missing evidence
- [ ] README explains how a future provider connector can replace only the model edge

## Claim this task
Post a short interface proposal before coding so parallel contributors can align.

tasks.title: [Docs] Run a newcomer test of the public contribution path
tasks.outcome: A friction log and focused documentation fixes
tasks.body:
## Goal
Pretend you are seeing the project for the first time. Follow README → challenge → safety/data rules → good first issue → PR guidance without using private context.

## Deliverable
Open a PR with a short friction log in `docs/onboarding-test.md` and fix the clearest documentation problems you found. Do not invent missing product behavior.

## Completion criteria
- [ ] Record browser/OS and access date
- [ ] Identify what was clear, confusing, missing, or contradictory
- [ ] Verify all public links you touched
- [ ] Keep fixes focused and accessible to non-experts

## Claim this task
Anyone may start this task; comment first to avoid duplicate reviews.
